title: Product Sans / Terminals
slide_intent: Treat stroke endings as part of a typeface’s voice because small angle choices alter openness and character.
strategic_value: Consistent open terminals can give Product Sans a recognizable character across otherwise geometric letters.
demonstration: A large two-row set of letters with visible open stroke endings sits above an explanation of terminal angles on blue.
practical_value: Inspect the endings across several letters together when judging whether a typeface’s construction is coherent.

content_islands.name: Terminal specimens

content_islands.name: Angle explanation
content_islands.spec: Place the construction note below at left, retaining its conditional language about 45-degree endings.

reference_purposes.Intent: The text identifies terminal angles as a distinguishing feature of geometric typefaces.
reference_purposes.Expression: The letter set demonstrates the open approach to stroke endings.
reference_purposes.Application: The note describes endings near 45 degrees where possible and cuts perpendicular to the stroke tangent.

ingredient.name: Open terminals
ingredient.role: Give the geometric letters a consistent open character.
ingredient.application: The specimen describes strokes ending at about 45 degrees where possible and terminals cut perpendicular to the stroke tangent.
ingredient.scope: A description of the designed Product Sans letterforms, not a universal exact-angle rule.
